case_studies.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
case_studies.abstract: Dispatch in three-sided marketplaces provides a natural setting for reinforcement learning from world feedback: decisions are evaluated by delayed operational outcomes such as delivery speed, courier utilization, and merchant congestion. We present a deployed reinforcement learning system at DoorDash that adapts dispatch objective weights in a large-scale food-delivery marketplace using delayed signals. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing dispatch decisions in three-sided marketplaces by using delayed feedback. The authors built a reinforcement learning system that adapts dispatch objective weights in a large-scale food-delivery marketplace. The result is a system that improves dispatch decisions using real-world data.

case_studies.title: Architecturally Significant MLOps Guidelines for ML Model Integration and Deployment: a Gray Literature Review
case_studies.abstract: Context. Despite the growing adoption of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps), teams often approach MLOps projects in an ad hoc manner due to the lack of consolidated architectural guidance. The community would benefit from a reference that synthesizes knowledge to inform the architectural design of MLOps systems, especially regarding the integration and deployment of ML models. Objective. In response, our goal is to provide a comprehensive overview of architecturally significant guidelines for the integration and deployment of ML models in MLOps systems. Method. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of lacking architectural guidance for Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) projects by providing a comprehensive overview of guidelines for integrating and deploying ML models. The authors built a reference guide that synthesizes knowledge from existing literature. The result is a set of guidelines that can inform the architectural design of MLOps systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for MLOps projects, here is what to do: review the guidelines for ML model integration and deployment, assess your current architecture against these guidelines, and update your design to ensure better model integration and deployment. This flags a risk: if your organisation uses ad hoc approaches to MLOps, check your current architecture for potential weaknesses immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those working on MLOps projects.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper discusses MLOps systems, providing guidelines for integration and deployment of ML models. This is relevant to IT systems and infrastructure. Novelty is moderate as it's a synthesis of existing knowledge, but still valuable. The focus on MLOps and deployment is highly relevant to IT teams.

case_studies.title: Zero Touch Predictive Orchestration: Automating Time-Series Models for the Cloud-Edge Continuum
case_studies.abstract: The Cloud-Edge Continuum (CEC) enables latency-critical applications by distributing resources to the far edge, but its extreme volatility makes proactive Zero Touch Management via time-series forecasting essential. However, orchestrators face a severe "cold start" problem: newly discovered nodes lack the historical data required to train localized predictive models, while generalized models fail to capture unique hardware and microservice behaviors. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of predicting resource needs in cloud-edge infrastructure by automating time-series models, the authors built a novel data-mixing methodology to train predictive models, and the result is a fully automated time-series prediction architecture. This technology can help with proactive management of cloud resources. It aims to improve the efficiency of cloud-edge continuum infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud-edge infrastructure, here is what to do: review your current predictive models, consider integrating automated time-series forecasting, and monitor the performance of your cloud resources to identify potential areas for improvement. This flags a risk: if your org uses generalized models, check their accuracy in capturing unique hardware and microservice behaviors immediately. If you are already using automated predictive models, assess whether this new methodology can enhance your existing setup.
